note: Precomputed by scripts/build_frontend_data.py; numbers come from the data files.

answers.question: How many experiments does this dashboard cover?
answers.answer: 403 tests from NASA PSI: 274 FLEX fuel-droplet tests (heptane and methanol) and 129 BASS-II solid-material tests, all run in microgravity on the ISS.

answers.question: Which tests match Earth / ISS cabin air (21% O2, 14.7 psi)?
answers.answer: 49 FLEX tests within ±1% O2 and ±0.5 psi of 21% / 14.7 psi (26 heptane, 23 methanol). BASS-II has no recorded pressure; 31 BASS-II tests match by O2 only.

answers.question: Are there tests at the expected Moon-base air (30% O2 or more, 10.2 psi or less)?
answers.answer: None exactly (0). With the tolerance (±0.5 psi) there are 17 FLEX tests at 10.33-10.5 psi and 30%-34% O2; outcomes: completion 2, disruption 15. The 30% / 10.2 psi figure is the challenge statement's estimate, not a NASA specification.

answers.question: Is there data for NASA's Exploration Atmosphere (8.2 psia, 34% O2)?
answers.answer: No data: no FLEX test is near 8.2 psi (the lowest is 10.18 psi). The closest tested condition is 34% O2 at 10.33-10.5 psi (n = 9), which is not the Exploration Atmosphere.

answers.question: Is there data for spacesuit conditions (100% O2, 4.3 psi)?
answers.answer: No data: the highest O2 tested is 34% and the lowest pressure is 10.18 psi.

answers.question: Which fuel burns faster, heptane or methanol?
answers.answer: Heptane has the higher mean burning rate in every O2 band (descriptive; pressures and suppressants mixed). O2 <0.15: heptane 0.455 mm2/s (n=4), methanol 0.38 mm2/s (n=21); O2 0.15-0.18: heptane 0.518 mm2/s (n=17), methanol 0.405 mm2/s (n=31); O2 0.18-0.21: heptane 0.491 mm2/s (n=34), methanol 0.465 mm2/s (n=38); O2 0.21-0.24: heptane 0.551 mm2/s (n=27), methanol 0.503 mm2/s (n=40); O2 >=0.24: heptane 0.644 mm2/s (n=25), methanol 0.613 mm2/s (n=21).

answers.question: What does 'disruption' mean in FLEX?
answers.answer: It is not defined in the FLEX Science Documents. 61 of 274 FLEX tests ended in 'disruption'; we do not interpret it further.

answers.question: Do CO2 or helium put out flames?
answers.answer: These data cannot show a causal effect: CO2 and He are confounded with O2 and FLEX chose conditions iteratively. Descriptive counts: none: 58/101 ended in extinction (57.4%), mean O2 0.207; co2: 88/123 ended in extinction (71.5%), mean O2 0.201; he: 40/50 ended in extinction (80.0%), mean O2 0.187.

answers.question: Which BASS-II materials were shown to burn?
answers.answer: Flame shown in at least one test: pmma_rod (n=54, 21 with outcome), pmma_thin_film (n=22, 4 with outcome), pmma_thick_sheet (n=20, 1 with outcome). Undetermined (no stated outcome): cotton_fiberglass_fabric (n=27), aramid_fabric (n=3), pmma_sphere (n=2), wax_candle (n=1). No material can be called non-flammable from these data.
warnings: Outcomes were extracted by AI; not_stated does not mean the flame did not go out.

answers.question: What happens to a fire in lunar gravity?
answers.answer: No data available for that question: every test here is in microgravity, and PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data yet. ACME's E-FIELD Flames only mimicked partial gravity with an electric field; it is an analog, not lunar data.
